title: Kataib Hezbollah Commander Accused of Planning Attacks on N.Y.C.
partialText: Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi is accused of directing and urging others to attack American and Israeli interests. Prosecutors say he is a leader of Kataib Hezbollah, an Iraqi militia with ties to Iran.

title: Trump Touts ‘Fantastic Trade Deals’ With China, but Details Are Scarce
partialText: The president left Beijing following a summit with China, during which the two countries sought to stabilize their economic and political relations.

title: Xi Pitches His Vision for Avoiding Conflict With the U.S.
partialText: Having fought the Trump administration to a draw, China’s Xi Jinping is proposing “constructive strategic stability,” aimed at drawing lines he thinks the U.S. should not cross.

title: Republicans Waited to Challenge Trump on the Iran War. Now It May Be Too Late.
partialText: Having deferred to the president for months, G.O.P. lawmakers missed crucial milestones to try to limit his war powers. That has tied their hands in seeking parameters and exit criteria.

title: Oil Prices Rise as Trump-Xi Summit Yields No Clear Breakthroughs on Iran War
partialText: Hopes for an end to the war in Iran faded after President Trump failed to secure a commitment from China to help persuade Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Justice Dept. Aims to Use Terrorism Laws to Target Mexican Officials
partialText: The Justice Department this week instructed federal prosecutors to build criminal drug cases against Mexican officials using new terrorism statutes.

title: How a Drug Cartel Made a Mexican State Its Tool
partialText: Cartel insiders say that in exchange for bribes and political support they were allowed to operate in Sinaloa state with near total freedom.

title: Archaeologists Find Egyptian Mummy Buried With the ‘Iliad’
partialText: For the deceased of Roman-era Egypt, Greek literature may have offered a cheat code to a more comfortable afterlife.

title: As Powell Steps Down, the Fed Confronts ‘Regime Change’
partialText: Jerome H. Powell is passing the chair’s baton to Kevin M. Warsh at the Federal Reserve, an institution that President Trump’s pick says needs an overhaul.

title: How Jerome Powell Managed a Chaotic Era
partialText: Our reporter Colby Smith, who covers the Federal Reserve and the economy, looks back at Jerome Powell’s tenure as chair of the Fed.

title: It’s Not Just U.S. Stocks. A.I. and Oil Are Moving Global Markets, Too.
partialText: Intel, along with Taiwan and South Korea, are the latest winners, our columnist says. True diversification is hard to find.

title: Martin Short and the Secret to Finding Joy While Surviving Tragedy
partialText: The comedy star, who is the subject of a new documentary, has faced a series of unimaginable losses. Yet he says there are always laughs to remember.

title: Deported Despite DACA: Dreamers Face Uncertainty Under Trump
partialText: The administration has said DACA isn’t a right to stay in the United States “indefinitely.” One man with DACA was detained and deported to Mexico in a matter of days.

title: Inside the Congolese Hotel Where Trump Deported 15 U.S. Migrants
partialText: They were shackled and sent to Kinshasa by the Trump administration. Now they face a dangerous choice: Go back to Latin America or stay in Africa.

title: German Chancellor, After Iran Spat With Trump, Reports ‘Good’ Phone Call
partialText: The call, initiated by Friedrich Merz, came soon after he told young people, “I am a great admirer of America. My admiration is not increasing at the moment.”

title: In Kentucky, the Iran War Complicates a Republican Primary
partialText: Representative Thomas Massie, the incumbent, has opposed President Trump’s military strikes on Iran. He is now facing the biggest challenge of his career.

title: Fierce Fights Over House Seats to Replace Nancy Pelosi and Jerrold Nadler
partialText: Nancy Pelosi and Jerrold Nadler are retiring, sparking fierce fights in San Francisco and Manhattan to succeed them. Whoever wins their seats could tap big donors and shape the Democratic Party.

title: Trump Loyalist Leads Administration’s Hunt for Fraud in Elections
partialText: The loyalist, Dan Bishop, put his fealty to the president on display when he pressed the F.B.I. to chase investigative leads it had already rejected.

title: Oysterman, Veteran, Prep-School Alum: A Senate Candidate’s Complex Class Story
partialText: Democrats are pinning their hopes of flipping the Senate on Graham Platner, who has made his working-class persona key to his campaign. His background defies easy categorization.

title: Why a Retrial of the Murdaugh Case Could Look a Lot Different
partialText: It is not clear when another trial would take place. But both prosecutors and defense lawyers said they would be forced to revise their legal strategies.

title: The Strange Alliance Trying to Remake American Psychiatry
partialText: The Department of Health and critical psychiatry activists are hoping to upend 40 years of medical orthodoxy.

title: Replacing a Royal Hand-Me-Down That Finally Frayed
partialText: Three years after King Charles III was crowned, the Royal Opera House in London hung plush new stage curtains bearing the monarch’s insignia — but only after the old ones gave up the ghost.

title: In Italy, Princess Catherine Puts Her Wardrobe to Work
partialText: Suits her, sir.

title: Inside the Secret Mission to Fly Taiwan’s President to Africa
partialText: From satellite phone check-ins to a borrowed royal plane, new details show how Taiwan’s leader’s team outwitted China and pulled off an audacious journey to southern Africa.

title: Why ‘Smart’ Products Have Started to Look Like the Dumb Choice
partialText: How Wi-Fi-connecting, app-based tech led to a backlash in the name of simplicity.

title: The Damage of ‘Trump Math’ Is Adding Up
partialText: Authoritarians go after data. The president has already started.

title: The Revolt Against the Girl Bosses Has Finally Come
partialText: Some of this country’s most prominent girl bosses sound like they don’t even know how to read the room.

title: At the Summit
partialText: We wrap up President Trump’s visit to China.

title: It’s a Hard Time to be a Young Adult. We Want to Hear From You.
partialText: I’m a Times reporter writing about young people in the New York City area. Whether you’re a young adult, or work with them, your insights can help.

title: Joe Sedelmaier, Auteur Behind ‘Where’s the Beef?’ Ad, Dies at 92
partialText: He directed nearly 1,000 comedic commercials, including a much-quoted spot for Wendy’s and one for FedEx featuring a manic speed talker.

title: Omaha Bar Is Not a Barbershop, State Barber Board Tells a Bar Named ‘Barber Shop’
partialText: The establishment changed its name this week from the Barber Shop Blackstone to the Censored Shop Blackstone in protest while it is suing the state in federal court.

title: Large Ebola Outbreak Is Declared in Congo
partialText: Dozens of deaths and hundreds of infections are suspected, an African agency said. Health experts were alarmed that the outbreak hadn’t been announced sooner.
